source.title: RML++: Regroup Median Loss for Combating Label Noise
source.authors: Feng-Peng Li; Ke-Mou Li; Qi-Zhou Wang; Bo Han; Jin-Yu Tian; Jian-Tao Zhou

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies symmetric label-noise rates and reports test accuracy for RML-trained models, bearing on the test-error trend in V4. It does not measure training error or test the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the memorization effect as motivation and uses loss-based sample selection, but does not test fitting completely random labels, shuffled or noise inputs, training time against true labels, explicit regularization, or learning order. Rows below cover only reported RML-Semi test accuracies under symmetric label noise; the paper does not report training error for these conditions.
record.test_reason: The study uses memorization and early learning of clean patterns to motivate a label-noise mitigation method. Its own results measure mitigation performance, loss separation and computational cost; they do not measure fitting corrupted labels or the order in which clean and noisy labels are learned. RML-Semi test accuracy across noise rates does not establish V4's joint prediction of perfect training fit and degrading generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that RML provides robust loss estimates and improves performance under label noise on synthetic and real-world datasets, with further improvements from its semi-supervised variant.
record.recipe_differences: RML changes loss processing and sample selection; RML-Semi adds semi-supervised training. It does not reproduce the original random-label fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and symmetric label-noise rate change reported test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports RML-Semi test accuracy decreasing from 96.5% to 95.7% to 93.9% on CIFAR-10 and from 78.9% to 77.8% to 64.1% on CIFAR-100 at symmetric noise rates 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8. Training error is unreported, and the method explicitly selects and relabels samples to mitigate noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RML-Semi retains substantial classification accuracy under increasing symmetric label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 and Section 3.4 describe separation of clean and noisy sample losses under RML versus cross-entropy. They do not report when the two groups are learned or whether noisy labels are eventually fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RML separates clean and noisy sample loss distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 7 compares methods at a fixed 50% symmetric noise rate; Figure 3 varies the RML median-window parameter. Neither compares time to fit true versus random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RML's computational cost and convergence depend on the training method and median-window setting.

record.problems: The relevant results report test accuracy but not training error, so they cannot establish whether the models fit the corrupted training labels perfectly. The rates are discrete rather than a continuous sweep, and the reported test accuracies remain well above chance.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained. Table 2 reports RML-Semi test accuracy across symmetric label-noise rates, but the study does not report the training-error outcome required by V4; V4 is therefore tested_not_extracted under the row requirements.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Perfect training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect fitting of corrupted training labels while test error increases toward chance across corruption rates from zero to complete randomization.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's T2 classification and V4 tested status: the reported noise-rate sweep evaluates mitigation performance. The baseline results in Tables 1–5 are attributed to prior studies. The abstract explicitly states that source code has been released.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or training hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time for true versus random labels and convergence versus corrupted-label fraction are not tested.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
Symmetric corruption rates and test accuracy are reported, but the reported training-error condition (perfect fitting) is not measured; near-chance test error is not reached in the reported settings.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and generalization after removing regularization are not tested as claim conditions.
The paper cites the memorization effect but does not measure learning order or compare learning of real versus random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
